challenge.reason: The old decision forbids writing secrets to .faff/ at all, not merely committing them; gitignore only addresses the commit path. The new decision writes literal API keys to .faff/cache/credentials.json, which directly contradicts the rule and adds a plaintext at-rest copy that outlives the process, can be read by other local tools, and can leak through backups, artefact uploads or log bundles. The why does not show that any premise of the old decision changed. The claimed benefit is also weak: process.env is already an in-memory lookup, so an in-process variable would give the same saving without touching disk. The supersession argument is unsound.
